items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: John Lee, the bassist, said, let’s do an album of Jobim’s music, and we did it.

ctx.x: Yeah. It was very impressive. I listened to it for a long time. I listened to it without trying to do anything with it. I just listened to it, because I loved listening to it. My mind got so far off into that, that I had to make myself start listening to something else. I was listening to Jobim. Finally, a couple of years ago, John Lee, the bassist, said, let’s do an album of Jobim’s music, and we did it. It was so inspiring to write the music – write the arrangements on that music. You just sat and listened to…
You’re doing your tenure with the Ferguson band. What essentially were you – what was your performance life like? Where were you playing? What kinds of gigs were you doing?

items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: This time will be Terrell Stafford, Antonio Hart, I think Renee Rosnes, John Lee and Dennis Mackrel.

ctx.x: And who is in that group now?
This time will be Terrell Stafford, Antonio Hart, I think Renee Rosnes, John Lee and Dennis Mackrel. And they’re giving us the best cabins on the boat.
All right. I like Antonio Hart. He reminds me of Cannonball some, who was my absolute hero.
